bet.text: A double intake on a swerve drive: easy to maneuver, with two sides that the team felt would pick up balls better.

demand.text: For the shooter the team picked field positions first. The one it knew was crucial was around the hangar, along with the protected shot: the robot could get away from defenders and have a free shot. A wall shot also helped, since it was harder for others to push the robot off course while shooting.

cycle.text: In an off-season interview: cargo enters from either side; rollers spin it to the center, where surgical tubing centers it and it goes up. An upper stage stops the ball at a sensor until the shooter is activated, and a lower stage holds another in a very similar way.

endgame.text: In an off-season interview: pneumatics pop the windmill up, and it spins as it lifts because the intakes block it. It latches onto the bar, spins up to mid, then goes up, spins back a little to release the right latch, and ends hanging vertical. Climbs are sometimes under about 10 seconds.

gave_up.text: The intakes block the climber, so it has to spin as it lifts (in an off-season interview).

changed.text: Backspin was an issue: opposite-spinning wheels were added just before Milford, unpowered, then powered almost directly after it. From an off-season interview, undated: a three-bar intake idea gave way to a four bar, and a lining stopped balls popping out; a gate came off the indexer; Motion Magic overshot and swung violently, so the climber spins to an angle and stops.

outcome.text: 49-18-0 in official play; finalist in the Roebling division; ranked 3 of the pooled top 20 (OPR 67.69, Roebling).
